item.title: Soft-confinement approximation of no-flux McKean-Vlasov dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.05431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the approximation of the no-flux McKean-Vlasov equation on a bounded convex domain by a whole-space equation with quadratic confinement of strength $\lambda^{-1}$ outside the domain. For a smooth bounded interaction kernel and a common bounded initial density with square-integrable gradient, we establish an $O(\lambda^{1/4})$ approximation rate. The estimate controls the $L^2$ density error uniformly on every finite time interval and the gradient error in space-time $L^2$. Without interaction, a spectral gap independent of $\lambda$ yields the $O(\lambda^{1/4})$ rate uniformly in time for the density error and uniformly over all unit time intervals for the gradient error. With interaction, we construct a counterexample showing that even weak convergence can fail to be uniform in time.
item.dc:creator: Geuntaek Seo, Yeoneung Kim, Beomjun Choi

item.title: On symmetry and monotonicity of singular solutions to critical fractional Hartree equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.05525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper continues the study initiated in \cite{GuJevnikarYang2026b} of fractional Hartree equations with zero capacity singular sets. We are concerned here with the critical case, i.e. \[ (-\Delta)^s u=\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\Gamma} \frac{u^{2_{\mu,s}^*}(y)}{|x-y|^\mu}\,d y\right)u^{2_{\mu,s}^*-1} \quad\text{in }\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\Gamma, \] where $N\ge2$, $s\in(0,1)$, $\mu\in(0,N)$ and $2_{\mu,s}^*$ is the critical exponent associated to this class of problems. We prove symmetry and monotonicity with respect to the singular set $\Gamma$. The Kelvin transforms centered at regular points provide sufficient decay at infinity for both the transformed solutions and their associated Hartree coefficients, without imposing global integrability assumptions. Combined with a moving plane argument and a comparison estimate in critical Lebesgue spaces, this allows the moving plane method to cover the full interaction range.
item.dc:creator: Guangze Gu, Aleks Jevnikar, Zhipeng Yang

item.title: One-third H\"older stability of optimal transport maps from log-concave sources
item.description:
arXiv:2611.05534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove quantitative stability of quadratic optimal transport maps from arbitrary log-concave sources to bounded targets. If the source $ho$ is isotropic on $\mathbb R^d$ and the targets $\mu$, $
u$ are supported in a common ball of radius $R$, their Brenier maps satisfy \[ \lVert T_\mu-T_
uVert_{L^2(ho)} \leqslant 17d^{2/3}R^{2/3}W_2(\mu,
u)^{1/3}. \] The one-third exponent is optimal for $d\geqslant2$. The proof combines a linear stability estimate for Brenier potentials in a weighted norm with a matching weighted reverse Poincar'e inequality. The weight is chosen in terms of the negative log-density of the source to account for its tails. We also show that the best dimensional constant in map stability is at least of order $d^{1/3}$.
item.dc:creator: Songbo Wang, Xiaozhen Wang

item.title: Continuity and Stability of the FitzHugh Nagumo System with Respect to the Diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2611.05770v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spatial heterogeneity in diffusion is a fundamental feature of excitable media, yet its effect on FitzHugh Nagumo dynamics remains mathematically challenging. We establish stability of solutions with respect to perturbations of the diffusion coefficient, providing a rigorous account of how changes in the medium affect the evolution of the system. Specifically, we prove a continuous dependence result ensuring that small perturbations in diffusion produce small variations in the corresponding solutions. The proof adapts the method of contracting rectangles to variable diffusion, yielding a framework for controlling and comparing solutions associated with different diffusion profiles. This result provides a rigorous link between heterogeneous and homogeneous FitzHugh Nagumo systems and justifies constant-diffusion approximations when the diffusion coefficient is close to a constant. Our analysis advances the understanding of FitzHugh Nagumo dynamics in heterogeneous media by establishing robustness with respect to spatial variations in diffusion.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Rodriguez

item.title: Existence of a Normalized Mountain Pass Solution for a Coupled Cubic Schr\"odinger System with Partial Confinement
item.description: arXiv:2611.05805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies a mass supercritical Schr\"odinger system with partial confinement: $$ \begin{cases} -\Delta u_1+|y|^2u_1 =\lambda_1u_1+\mu_1u_1^3+2\beta u_1u_2^2,\qquad x\in\R^3,\\ -\Delta u_2+|y|^2u_2 =\lambda_2u_2+\mu_2u_2^3+2\beta u_1^2u_2,\qquad x\in\R^3, \end{cases} $$ subject to the mass constraints $ \int_{\R^3}u_1^2\dd x=a_1$, $\int_{\R^3}u_2^2\dd x=a_2,$ where $x=(y,z)\in\R^2\times\R$, the parameters $\mu_1,\mu_2,\beta$ are positive, and $\lambda_1,\lambda_2\in\R$ are unknown Lagrange multipliers. The masses satisfy $(a_1,a_2)=\eps(\rho_1,\rho_2)$ for a fixed vector $\rho=(\rho_1,\rho_2)\in (0,\infty)^2$. For all sufficiently small $\eps>0$, we establish the existence of a positive normalized solution $u_\eps^-$ at a mountain pass level on the full product mass sphere. This level coincides with the infimum of the energy over the negative part of the Pohozaev set. The main difficulty arises from the lack of compactness due to partial confinement. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a compactness argument that preserves the two independent mass constraints and show that every minimizing sequence for this infimum admits a strongly convergent subsequence after suitable common translations along the unconfined axial direction. We further establish the asymptotic relation $\eps E(u_\eps^-)\to m_0(\rho)$ as $\varepsilon\to0$, where $m_0(\rho)>0$ denotes the infimum of the free energy under the corresponding Pohozaev constraint. In addition, we derive the asymptotic behavior of the kinetic and potential energies. The solution obtained here is distinct from the normalized ground states constructed by Jia et al. [Discrete Contin. Dyn. Syst., 40(2020), 2739-2766] through local minimization for sufficiently small masses.
item.dc:creator: Wan-Yue Tang, Hong-Rui Sun, Jianlun Liu

item.title: Analysis of a Two Membrane Thermoelastic Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.05819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate and study a mathematical model of a thermoforming process involving two interdependent thermoelastic membranes coupled with equations governing heat transfer. These membranes interact with each other through means of elastic forces and thermal transfer which determines changes in elastic properties and further deform the membranes. The two thermoelastic membranes lead to a pair of implicit obstacle problems which are modeled both as a 2-membrane problem or a pair of quasi-variational inequalities. Mathematically, the primary model couples an elliptic two membrane problem with associated nonlinear elliptic equations describing temperature distribution. We show, under physically relevant conditions, the existence of solutions via a fixed point approach that involves reformulation of the problem to improve regularity of solutions.
item.dc:creator: Nathaniel J. Fink-Humes, Carlos N. Rautenberg

item.title: Observability and stabilizability for Grushin-Type parabolic equations in the whole space
item.description: arXiv:2611.05821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study observability and stabilization for the whole-space Grushin heat equation $$ \partial_t u-\Delta_\gamma u=0,\qquad \Delta_\gamma:=\Delta_x+|x|^{2\gamma}\Delta_y,\qquad (t,x,y)\in(0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m,\quad \gamma>0. $$ For product sets $E=E_1\times E_2$, we identify three observability regimes in which thickness, distance from the degeneracy set $\{x=0\}$, and local density near that set play different roles. (i) In the subcritical regime $0<\gamma<1$, the observability inequality holds for every $T>0$ if and only if both $E_1$ and $E_2$ are thick; hence $T_{\min}(E)=0$. (ii) At the critical exponent $\gamma=1$, if $E_2=\mathbb{R}^m$ and $E_1\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is thick, we determine the exact minimal observable time: $$ T_{\min}(E)=\frac{a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1)^2}{2n},\qquad a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1):=\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_{x\in E_1}|x|. $$ Thus, the threshold depends on the essential distance of $E_1$ from the degeneracy set. (iii) In the supercritical regime $\gamma>1$, we consider $n=1$, $E_2=\mathbb{R}^m$ and thick sets $E_1\subset\mathbb{R}$. If $a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1)>0$, observability fails for every $T>0$, so that $T_{\min}(E)=+\infty$. If $a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1)=0$, observability depends on the density of $E_1$ near $0$, measured by $$ D_{E_1}(r):=\log\!\left(\frac{2r}{|E_1\cap(-r,r)|}\right),\qquad L_{E_1}:=\limsup_{r\downarrow0}r^2D_{E_1}(r). $$ If $L_{E_1}=0$, then $T_{\min}(E)=0$; if $0<L_{E_1}<\infty$, a finite sufficient observation time exists. Moreover, observability at time $T$ requires $$ \limsup_{r\downarrow0}r^{2(1+\gamma)/(\gamma-1)}D_{E_1}(r)\le C_{T,\gamma}. $$ In contrast, for every $\gamma>0$, exponential and complete stabilizability hold if and only if both $E_1$ and $E_2$ are thick. The stabilization criterion is therefore independent of $\gamma$.
item.dc:creator: Shanlin Huang, Gengsheng Wang, Jiaqi Yu

item.title: Effect of a fourth-order diffusion term on the robustness of the transfer function stability for hyperbolic systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.05845v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a $2\times2$ hyperbolic system with anti-located control and observation. It is well known that the system can be stabilized with a delayed output-feedback control and that, unfortunately, this design is arbitrarily sensitive to small errors in the transport velocity. It was recently proved that adding a second-order diffusion term to the system restores robustness. We show that the same phenomenon occurs with a fourth-order diffusion term: the maximal spectral abscissa of the closed-loop system converges, as the diffusion parameter goes to zero, to the explicit value $-\ln(2)$, and the resulting stability margin is robust to small perturbations of the transport velocity. This additional term leads to a quartic characteristic equation whose roots have no tractable closed-form expression. We develop an asymptotic classification of its four roots and use it to obtain a first-order expansion of the transfer function with an explicit error bound. Combining this expansion with a topological degree argument, we show that $-\ln(2)$ is in fact the exact limiting value of the spectral abscissa, extending to the fourth-order case the sharpness result previously available only for second-order diffusive terms.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Cerpa, Felipe Labra

item.title: Failure of superharmonicity near an isolated singularity of the critical biharmonic equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.05998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $n\ge5$ and $u$ be a positive singular solution of $\Delta^2u=u^{(n+4)/(n-4)}$ in a punctured ball. A long-standing question is where or not $ -\Delta u>0$ in the punctured ball. In this paper we show that the answer is negative. More precisely we construct a positive singular solution whose singularity at the origin is nonremovable, while its lower limit there is zero. On a normal subspace, $-\Delta u$ converges to a strictly negative constant. The spherical minimum has order $r^\beta$, where $2<\beta<4$, and the spherical Harnack ratio is unbounded. The proof uses balanced planar polygons, finitely many exterior parameters and a countable gluing construction.
item.dc:creator: Juncheng Wei, Hui Yang, Ronghao Yang

item.title: The Maximum Principle and Optimal Gradient Estimates of Solutions to the Insulated Conductivity Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.06016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the insulated conductivity problem with two unit spherical inclusions embedded in a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\ge3$. The gradient of solutions may blow up as the distance between the two inclusions goes to zero. We introduce bispherical coordinates and expand the solution in spherical harmonics. Then we use the maximum principle to give a new proof of the optimal gradient estimate obtained by Dong-Li-Yang.
item.dc:creator: Saibo Chen

item.title: Constrained minimization problem and unbounded dynamics for the four-dimensional Klein-Gordon-Schr\"{o}dinger System
item.description: arXiv:2611.06094v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the Klein-Gordon-Schrodinger system in four spatial dimensions. We consider a constrained minimization problem associated with the corresponding stationary system and establish the existence of a positive radial minimizer. We further investigate the asymptotic behavior and qualitative properties of minimizers. As an application, we analyze the dynamics of solutions with initial data in a potential well and prove that such solutions either blow up in finite time or exhibit unbounded growth in the energy norm as time tends to infinity. Since the minimizers lie on the boundary of the potential well, we also establish the strong instability of the associated standing waves.
item.dc:creator: Masaru Hamano, Hiroaki Kikuchi, Kenta Tomioka

item.title: A Viscous Cascade Construction of Nonunique Leray--Hopf Solutions to the Unforced 3D Navier--Stokes Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.06117v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a nonzero divergence-free initial velocity on $\mathbb{R}^3$ and a continuum of pairwise distinct suitable Leray--Hopf solutions of the unforced three-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations on a common time interval. The initial datum is axisymmetric, smooth away from the origin, and belongs to every $L^{\mathfrak q}$ with $1\leq \mathfrak q<3$, but not to $L^3$. All the solutions attain this datum strongly in $L^2$, are smooth at positive times, and satisfy both the global and local energy equalities through time zero. The same family belongs simultaneously to every $L^{\mathfrak p}_tL^{\mathfrak q}_x$ with $1\leq \mathfrak p\leq\infty$, $2\leq \mathfrak q\leq\infty$, and $2/\mathfrak p+3/\mathfrak q>1$. The same solutions also belong to the critical Lorentz space $L^\infty_tL^{3,\infty}_x$. This endpoint is sharp for uniqueness in the Leray--Hopf class within the Lorentz scale. The proof is entirely analytic and uses a cascade through geometrically separated Gaussian swirls. We establish growth for the time-dependent viscous linearization and determine the sign of its complete quadratic stress, including the interaction of the reference velocity with the second variation. The integrated stress generates a controlled perturbation at the next larger spatial scale. At each finite cutoff, a prescribed terminal coordinate selects an initial perturbation whose physical $L^2$ norm tends to zero as the cutoff is removed. Uniform energy, moment, and transfer estimates yield the common strong initial trace while preserving a nonzero observable at a fixed positive time.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Y. Hou, Xiang Qin, Peicong Song, Wenhan Zhang

item.title: Dispersion of Magnetic Coriolis Waves
item.description: arXiv:2611.06200v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the 3-D rotating magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) equations. The combination of rotation and background magnetic field leads to the occurrence of dispersive magneto-Coriolis waves in the linearized equations. We establish a t ^{-1} decay estimate for waves with dispersion relation $\sigma$($\xi$) = $\xi$ \_3 h(|$\xi$|) under suitable assumptions on h, and show that this includes magneto-Coriolis waves. Then we apply these dispersive estimates to the nonlinear rotating MHD equations and obtain an improved lower bound on the lifespan of solutions.
item.dc:creator: Niklas Knobel (ICJ), Zhuoya Yao (ICJ)

item.title: Sharp asymptotic stability of the IPM equation in $\mathbb{R}^2$ via isopycnal coordinates
item.description: arXiv:2611.06241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the incompressible porous media (IPM) equation, a model describing the motion of a fluid with variable density through a porous medium under the action of gravity. We prove that the stably stratified state, in which heavier fluid lies below lighter fluid, is nonlinearly stable: small perturbations decay over time and the fluid returns to equilibrium. Our result holds in the sharp Sobolev setting $H^s(\mathbb R^2)$ for every $s>2$: this threshold cannot be improved, since the equation is ill-posed in $H^2(\mathbb R^2)$. This result follows from a proof of global well-posedness at critical Besov regularity, with smallness required only in a norm invariant under the natural scaling of the equation. We also prove optimal decay rates for suitably localized initial data. The main difficulty is that the stabilizing effect of stratification acts only in some directions, while the nonlinear transport acts in all of them. Reaching the sharp regularity threshold requires two main novelties. First, we rewrite the equation in \emph{isopycnal coordinates}, which follow the level sets of the density: in these coordinates the transport becomes one-dimensional, and the anisotropic stabilizing mechanism can be exploited at minimal regularity. Second, we establish new \emph{anisotropic commutator estimates} which allow us to control the remaining nonlinear terms. Finally, we show that the estimates obtained in isopycnal coordinates can be transferred back to the original variables.
item.dc:creator: Roberta Bianchini, Timoth\'ee Crin-Barat, Ling-Yun Shou, Shan Wang

item.title: From Continuum-Kinematics-Inspired Peridynamics to Simplicial Hyperelasticity
item.description: arXiv:2611.06242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a variational and functional-analytic framework for continuum-kinematics-inspired peridynamics with simultaneous nonlocal interactions among multiple points. We encode the finite-difference data of each interacting simplex in a simplicial deformation gradient. For nondegenerate simplices in three dimensions, the gradient, its cofactor, and its determinant encode the associated continuum-kinematics-inspired peridynamic line, area, and volume changes, respectively. This unified representation leads to a class of simplicial hyperelastic energies with general, possibly nonadditive, constitutive dependence on the affine deformation of an interacting simplex, thereby extending the original continuum-kinematics-inspired peridynamic framework. To describe interactions occurring at different scales and over different simplex geometries, we introduce radial- and shape-weighted nonlocal spaces. Their multipoint seminorms control two-point energies induced by the edge marginals of the interaction measure. This comparison yields nonlocal Poincar\'e inequalities and fractional Sobolev embeddings. We establish existence of equilibrium configurations by two complementary mechanisms. Particle-wise averaged convexity yields weak lower semicontinuity of the associated energy functionals. Under stronger assumptions on the edge marginals, fractional compactness gives existence for nonconvex energy densities. These results provide a mathematical foundation for simplicial and continuum-kinematics-inspired peridynamic models.
item.dc:creator: Anton Evgrafov, Pablo Pedregal

item.title: Classification of radially symmetric solutions to a Hardy-H{\'e}non equation with sublinear absorption and applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.06276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uniqueness of a non-negative radially symmetric solution with non-increasing profile to the Hardy-H{\'e}non elliptic equation with sublinear absorption \\ ____________ $\Delta$v(x) + |x|\textsuperscript{$\sigma$}v(x) - v\textsuperscript{1/m}(x)=0, ______ x$\in$___\textsuperscript{N}, \\ is established in the range N$\ge$1, m>1 and $\sigma$$\in$(max{-2,-N},0). Consequences of this result are the uniqueness (up to scaling) of the non-negative extremal function to a Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequality and the uniqueness of a non-negative radially symmetric self-similar solution with nonincreasing profile to a parabolic Hardy-H{\'e}non equation with quasilinear diffusion. The proof relies on ordinary differential equations techniques, which can be used thanks to the radially symmetric setting, and requires in particular a delicate analysis of the well-posedness and continuous dependence in view of the non-Lipschitz nonlinearity and the singularity of |x|\textsuperscript{$\sigma$} at the origin.
item.dc:creator: Razvan Gabriel Iagar (URJC), Philippe Lauren\c{c}ot (LAMA)

item.title: Large time behavior of global solutions to one-dimensional non-isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations with large initial data
item.description: arXiv:2611.06309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we are concerned with the construction of global solutions to the Cauchy problem for the one-dimensional non-isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations, as well as the precise description of their large-time behavior. While results for small initial data are well-established, the case of large initial perturbations remains less satisfactory. Even for constant transport coefficients, only the Nishida-Smoller type solutions have been obtained so far. In this work, we will provide a complete resolution of this problem. The key idea involves revealing favorable hidden identities of the potential force and a new representation for the specific volume, which enables us to derive uniform upper and lower bounds on this quantity. Moreover, this strategy extends to compressible viscous single-ion flow under the Boltzmann relation; notably, this new method for deriving lower and upper bounds on the specific volume also applies to the Navier-Stokes equations. The proof relies on a domain decomposition technique and some new dissipative structures to close the nonlinear energy estimates.
item.dc:creator: Lan Zhang, Huijiang Zhao

item.title: Normal form smoothing and spatial analyticity for the dispersion-generalized periodic KdV equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.06313v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the persistence of spatial analyticity for solutions to the dispersion-generalized periodic Korteweg-de Vries equation $$\partial_tu-\partial_x|D_x|^\alpha u+u\partial_xu=0,\qquad\alpha\ge2.$$ For real-valued initial data $u_0\in G^{\sigma_0,s}(\mathbb T)$, with $\sigma_0>0$ and $s\ge-\alpha/4$, we prove that the corresponding global solution satisfies $$u\in C([-T,T];G^{\sigma(T),s}(\mathbb T)),\qquad\sigma(T)=\min\left\{\sigma_0,\frac cT\right\},$$ for every $T>0$. As a consequence, our result improves the lower bound for the radius of spatial analyticity established by Himonas, Kalisch, and Selberg (2017) for $2\le\alpha<4$, including the classical periodic KdV equation, and establishes a unified $T^{-1}$ lower bound for the analyticity radius for every $\alpha\ge2$. The main novelties are twofold. First, we introduce a normal form reduction at the level of the Gevrey energy, which reveals an additional cancellation in the cubic Gevrey commutator and separates it into a non-accumulating boundary correction and a quartic remainder. Second, we establish a global-in-time periodic $L_{t,x}^4$ estimate for the non-polynomial phase $k|k|^\alpha$, valid for every real $\alpha\ge2$. Together, these ingredients yield a refined almost conservation law and the $T^{-1}$ lower bound for the radius of spatial analyticity.
item.dc:creator: Jaeseop Ahn, Chulkwang Kwak

item.title: Generalized principal eigenvalues for nonlocal operators with drift
item.description: arXiv:2611.06316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlocal diffusion operators with a drift term naturally arise in models such as moving coordinate systems induced by climate change. This paper systematically studies several concepts of generalized principal eigenvalues (GPEs) for such operators. We allow the dispersal kernel to be heterogeneous and non-symmetric, and remove the standard global upper bound on the kernel (thereby covering the case of heavy-tailed dispersal kernels). To overcome the analytical difficulties brought by this more general setting, we establish a new Harnack-type inequality for non-compactly supported kernels, and apply homogenization and cut-off approximation techniques to derive two-sided bounds for the domain approximation limit of GPEs. Furthermore, under the almost periodic setting, we prove that the GPEs defined through different admissible test function spaces (e.g., \(C^1\) spaces with bounded derivatives and uniformly continuous function spaces in the viscosity sense) are completely coincident. This characterization reveals a fundamental unification: the limit result of principal eigenvalues under domain approximation by Coville and Hamel coincides exactly with the explicit variational formula by Du, Fang, and Ni, thereby bridging two previously independent theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Hailin Tong, Tao Zhou

item.title: Second critical exponent for a quasilinear Hardy--H\'enon equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.06318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for the parabolic Hardy--H\'enon equation $\partial_tu=\Delta u^m+|x|^\sigma u^p$ with slow diffusion $m>1$ and a potential which is singular at the origin, $-2<\sigma<0$, in dimension $N\ge3$. Above the Fujita exponent, global and blowing-up solutions coexist, and we show that the spatial decay of the initial data decides between them. The second critical exponent turns out to be the decay rate of an explicit singular steady state. Data decaying more slowly blow up in finite time, whatever their size, while faster decaying data which are small in a weighted supremum norm give rise to global solutions. At the critical decay, and in the range where the singular steady state exists, we construct bounded stationary barriers with exactly critical tail by gluing the singular steady state to regular steady states. We deduce that the critical amplitude separating global existence from blow-up lies between the amplitude of the singular steady state and an explicit constant. We also show that data lying below a proper fraction of the singular steady state produce global bounded solutions, and that the singular amplitude itself is attained by global solutions whenever a Joseph--Lundgren type condition fails. Conjectures and open problems complete the picture.
item.dc:creator: Rihab Ben Belgacem, Mohamed Majdoub

item.title: One-dimensional nodal solutions of the Lane--Emden problem in cylinders: asymptotic behaviour and energy stability
item.description: arXiv:2611.06339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Lane-Emden problem $-\Delta u=|u|^{p-1}u$, $p>1$, in bounded domains of a half-cylinder $\omega\times(0,+\infty)$, with Dirichlet conditions on the relative boundary and Neumann conditions on the boundary of the cylinder. In flat cylinders $\omega\times(0,L)$ this problem admits, for every $p>1$, one-dimensional solutions with any prescribed number $m$ of nodal regions. We study the stability of these domains, as critical points of a related energy functional, with respect to volume-preserving deformations of the domain. We prove that, for $p$ large, the flat cylinders are stable as soon as their height exceeds a threshold growing linearly in $p$, while, for $p$ close to $1$, both stability and instability occur, with explicit thresholds depending on $m$ and on the first nontrivial Neumann eigenvalue of $\omega$. These results rely on a detailed analysis of the one-dimensional profiles: we describe their asymptotic behaviour, and that of the first eigenvalue of the associated linearized operator, as $p\to1^+$ and $p\to+\infty$, we obtain expansions of the amplitude with explicit constants, and we prove global comparison results with respect to $p$, some of which are new also for positive solutions.
item.dc:creator: Francesca De Marchis, Lisa Mazzuoli

item.title: The Kato square root property for fractional elliptic operators in divergence form
item.description:
arXiv:2611.06391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the Kato square root property for fractional elliptic operators $L = -\operatorname{div}^\alpha(\mu 
abla^\alpha \cdot)$ of order $2\alpha \in (0,2)$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, built from the Riesz fractional gradient and divergence, with bounded, measurable and uniformly elliptic complex coefficients $\mu$. More precisely, we show that the domain of $L^{1/2}$ coincides with the distributional fractional Sobolev space $\mathrm{S}^{\alpha,2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and that $\|L^{1/2} u\|_{\mathrm{L}^2} \simeq \|
abla^\alpha u\|_{\mathrm{L}^2}$, with constants that are locally uniform in $\alpha$. As a consequence, we recover the Kato square root property for elliptic operators $-\operatorname{div}(\mu
abla\cdot)$ in the limit $\alpha 	o 1$, and we obtain continuity of the square root with respect to the parameter $\alpha$. The proof follows the second-order approach to the Kato problem. Its two new ingredients are nonlocal off-diagonal estimates of polynomial order for the resolvents of $L$, and a construction of $T(b)$-test functions that circumvents the nonlocality of $
abla^\alpha$ by factorizing it through Riesz potentials.
item.dc:creator: Luca Haardt

item.title: Positive coexistence solutions for systems of multi-kernel Hammerstein type equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.06536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate positive solutions with both components nontrivial for systems of Hammerstein integral equations associated with a general $2\times2$ matrix of Green's kernels, thereby extending the decoupled (diagonal) case to systems with cross-coupling. Such systems arise from boundary value problems in which the unknowns may be coupled both in the differential equations and in the boundary conditions, a setting that has received considerably less attention than the decoupled case. Using a component-wise Krasnosel'ski\u{\i} compression--expansion fixed point theorem in product cones, we derive existence and non-existence criteria. A multiplicity result guaranteeing at least two positive solutions is also obtained, by means of the fixed point index in cones. As an application, we consider radially symmetric solutions for an elliptic system on an annulus with coupled Robin boundary conditions.
item.dc:creator: Laura M. Fern\'andez-Pardo, Jorge Rodr\'iguez-L\'opez

item.title: Asymptotic behavior of generic Riemann solutions to one-dimensional full compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.06560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the time-asymptotic stability of the one-dimensional full compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations, assuming that the corresponding quasi-neutral Euler equations admit a generic Riemann solution consisting of a shock, a contact discontinuity, and a rarefaction wave. It is proved that there exists a unique global-in-time solution, which converges in $L^\infty$ norm, as time goes to infinity, to the ansatz composed of a viscous shock with a time-dependent shift, a viscous contact wave, and an inviscid rarefaction wave. The main difficulty arises from the non-conservative lower-order source terms induced by the electric potential in the momentum and energy equations, which significantly complicates the proof of the existence of individual waves (especially the viscous shock) and the derivation of the relative entropy estimates. To overcome this, we make full use of the Poisson equation satisfied by the electric potential, and combine the weighted relative entropy method with the $a$-contraction method with shifts to close the estimates within the $H^2$-perturbation framework.
item.dc:creator: Xin-Xiang Bian, Jiajin Shi, Lingling Xie

item.title: Construction of entropies for cross-diffusion systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.06578v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The analysis of cross-diffusion systems with nonsymmetric and indefinite diffusion matrices often relies on the existence of entropies, that is, Lyapunov functionals whose dissipation often yields gradient estimates. We propose a general strategy for constructing entropies for two-species cross-diffusion systems, based on the assumption that the mobility matrix is symmetric, in accordance with Onsager's reciprocal relations. The symmetry condition leads to a linear hyperbolic equation in two variables, which can be reformulated as a linear transport system along the eigendirections of the diffusion matrix, related to the approach of Jenssen and Kogan for hyperbolic conservation laws. Positive solutions to this system yield a family of entropies parametrized by two arbitrary functions of one variable. Sufficient conditions for their existence on (possibly unbounded) characteristic rectangles are given, the mechanisms that may prevent the existence of an entropy are identified, and systems without any entropy structure are presented. The general construction recovers known entropies for models arising in physics and biology and provides new ones. For systems with an arbitrary number of components, we derive sufficient conditions for the existence of separable entropies and give a rank criterion for the uniqueness of entropies (up to affine functions). Cross-diffusion systems without symmetry of the mobility matrix are also discussed.
item.dc:creator: Xiuqing Chen, Ansgar J\"ungel, Mingyue Zhang

item.title: Unique continuation, nonexistence and bubbling for the critical $p$-Laplace equation II: the degenerate elliptic case and higher dimensions
item.description:
arXiv:2611.06694v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every $p>1$, we prove that a nontrivial solution of  egin{equation*} -\Delta_pu=f(x,u,
abla u) \end{equation*} in a planar domain, with $|f(x,s,\xi)|\leq C(|s|^{p-1}+|\xi|^{p-1})$, vanishes neither on an open set nor to infinite order at a point. This allows us to prove unique continuation properties of axially symmetric solutions to $p$-Laplace equations in higher dimensions $N\geq3$, with axially symmetric $p$-harmonic functions as a particular case. Unlike in our previous work, the analysis is based here on the regularity and quasiconformal properties of the whole stress field $|
abla u|^{p-2}
abla u$ in the plane, taking into account the more delicate regularity theory for $p>2$. This allows us to prove Liouville-type and bubble profile decomposition results for critical problems in dimensions $N\geq3$ and in the whole range $1<p<N$, under some symmetry conditions.
item.dc:creator: Carlo Mercuri

item.title: Evolution Dynamics and Cauchy Problems with Quaternionic Variables and Lifting to Banach Bilateral $\mathbb{A}$-Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.06721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop a theory of evolution dynamics in a Banach bilateral $\mathbb{H}$-algebra and establish a well-posedness theory for the Cauchy problem of evolution equations with quaternionic variables. First, we study the geometric properties of slice structures of Banach bilateral $\mathbb{H}$-modules. By employing different slice structures, we construct some noncommutative Banach bilateral $\mathbb{H}$-subalgebras which are compatible with the slice regularity of the functions involved. Moreover, through the quaternionic sliced geometric path integral over Banach bilateral $\mathbb{A}$-module, an integral representation of the solution to the homogeneous Cauchy problem with quaternionic variables is obtained in a quaternionic $\sigma$-ball, and for the first time, a local existence and uniqueness theorem is established for $\sigma$-analytic solutions. Then the local $\sigma$-analytic solution is extended to the entire quaternionic spherical sectorial region, thereby proving a global existence and uniqueness theorem for the Cauchy problem. Based on it, the notion of an evolution system in a quaternionic $\mathbb{H}$-algebra is introduced and its core properties are established. In addition, the global existence and uniqueness theorems are obtained under hyperbolic-like and parabolic-like conditions. Finally, the structure of Banach bilateral $\mathbb{H}$-modules and $\mathbb{H}$-algebras is lifted to Banach bilateral $\mathbb{A}$-modules and $\mathbb{A}$-algebras, and a well-posedness theory for evolution equations in this setting is developed. This reveals, from a new perspective, the universality of well-posedness for the Cauchy problem under the generic noncommutative $\mathbb{A}$-algebraic structures.
item.dc:creator: Chao Wang, Guangzhou Qin, Jibin Li

item.title: Finite-Time Blowup for Navier-Stokes with Smooth Forcing, Part II: Residual Correction via Oscillatory Pulses
item.description: arXiv:2611.06869v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is a companion to Part I: Construction of Self-Similar Solutions with Admissible Stress and Flat Remainder (arXiv:2609.35406). Part I constructs approximately self-similar flow profiles with a singular stress in divergence form. The associated velocity becomes unbounded as $t\uparrow 1$. Here, localized oscillatory pulses cancel this stress contribution through their averaged quadratic momentum flux. Successive corrections preserve the velocity growth and leave a smooth external force $f\in C^\infty$. This gives a local solution of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with forcing $f$. Its velocity satisfies $\limsup_{t\uparrow 1}\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}=\infty$. Together, the two papers present a readable and accessible account of OpenAI's Finite Time Blowup for Navier-Stokes. We claim no original mathematical contribution.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Lei, Xiao Ren

item.title: Variational exponential estimates and stationary large deviations for SPDEs
item.description: arXiv:2611.05830v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish an abstract criterion for large deviations of invariant measures when the deterministic dynamics has a single globally attracting equilibrium. Deterministic regularisation and attraction yield an endpoint estimate for long controlled paths of bounded action, uniformly over each fixed bounded initial set. This allows the finite time Freidlin-Wentzell uniform LDP on bounded initial sets to be combined directly with stationary exponential norm estimates. The proof requires neither a separate exponential tightness argument nor a Dembo-Zeitouni uniform LDP, and imposes no decay condition on differences between controlled trajectories. Finite path approximation identifies the quasipotential as the good rate function. We also establish a variational criterion based on the Bou\'e-Dupuis representation that derives exponential estimates from bounds for controlled outputs, without requiring their convergence. Uniform controlled terminal moments yield estimates uniform in time, which pass to Krylov-Bogoliubov invariant measures. Together, these results establish stationary LDPs in four regimes: two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations with possibly unbounded, globally Lipschitz, uniformly positive scalar amplitudes and vanishing noise correlation; reaction-diffusion systems without the additional restriction linking noise growth to reaction strength; Allen-Cahn equations with opposite boundary values and globally Lipschitz, uniformly nondegenerate multiplicative space-time white noise on intervals of arbitrary length; and Burgers equations with fixed covariance $(-\Delta)^\alpha$, $0\leq\alpha<1/2$. For Burgers, we also obtain Gaussian norm estimates.
item.dc:creator: Rui Bai, Chunrong Feng, Huaizhong Zhao

item.title: BMV conjecture and positivity of spectral shift for relatively Schatten perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2611.05879v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish BMV-type results and prove the positivity-preserving property and uniqueness of support-normalized spectral shift functions of arbitrary order for semibounded operators with relatively Schatten-von Neumann perturbations. We also derive correlation inequalities in the relative Hilbert-Schmidt case. These results build on a new positivity-preserving property for the trace of a higher-order operator derivative along a relatively Schatten direction and are obtained using methods of multilinear operator integration and approximation.
item.dc:creator: Chandan Pradhan, Anna Skripka

item.title: Parabolic Extrapolation of Compactness with Applications to Characterizations of the Parabolic CMO Space via Parabolic Fractional Commutators
item.description: arXiv:2611.05933v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this article, we prove two compactness parabolic extrapolation theorems for linear operators and their commutators on parabolic weighted Lebesgue spaces. As applications, we show that $b\in\mathrm{PCMO}$ (parabolic CMO space) if and only if $b\in L_\mathrm{loc}^1$ and the commutator $[b,I_\alpha^{\gamma+}]_k$ is compact from $L^r(\omega^r)$ to $L^q(\omega^q)$ for any $k\in\mathbb{N}$, $1<r<q<\infty$ with $\frac{1}{r}-\frac{1}{q}=\alpha\in(0,1)$, and $\omega\in A_{r,q}^+(\gamma)$ (parabolic Muckenhoupt class), where $I_\alpha^{\gamma+}$ is the parabolic fractional integral. Several other equivalent characterizations of the space $\mathrm{PCMO}$ are also given. Our approach combines the unweighted compactness for mixed commutators, a local lower estimate for $[b,I_\alpha^{\gamma+}]_k$, and both a quantitative Uchiyama-type description and the equivalence with $\inf_T\{\|[\cdot,I_\alpha^{\gamma+}]_k-T\|_{L^r\to L^q}^\frac{1}{k}\}$ of $\mathrm{dist}_{\mathrm{PBMO}}(\cdot,\mathrm{PCMO})$, where the infimum is taken over all compact operators $T:L^r\to L^q$. Finally, we establish two parabolic weighted Fr\'echet--Kolmogorov compactness criteria, which further induce a parabolic interpolation theorem of compactness.
item.dc:creator: Mingming Cao, Weiyi Kong, Dachun Yang, Wen Yuan, Chenfeng Zhu

item.title: Reconstruction and well-posedness of an inverse coefficient problem for a diffusion equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.06112v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work, we investigate the inverse coefficient problem of determining an unknown coefficient in a diffusion equation from a single boundary flux measurement. More precisely, assuming that the domain is cylindrical, we develop a unified theoretical and numerical framework for the stable reconstruction of a space-time-dependent coefficient, by reformulating the inverse problem as a nonlinear equation. The inherent nonlinearity of the problem is transferred to an auxiliary nonlinear equation, enabling the application of techniques and concepts from nonlinear analysis. By combining representation formulas with regularity properties of solutions to diffusion equations, we extend to nonlinear inverse problems an approach that has so far been restricted to linear ones. The theoretical reconstruction procedure is complemented by a numerical analysis of the proposed method, including convergence and error estimates, as well as numerical experiments. The proposed reconstruction algorithm is directly inspired by the theoretical framework.
item.dc:creator: Siyu Cen, Bangti Jin, Yavar Kian, Zhi Zhou

item.title: Existence of Lagrangian Mean Curvature Flow Singularities with Bounded Mean Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2611.06248v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In every dimension $n \ge 3$, we show there exist Lagrangian mean curvature flows that develop neck pinch singularities such that the mean curvature remains uniformly bounded. This follows from a related result that, under a structural assumption on the singularity formation, the mean curvature at small scales near the singularity can be bounded by the Lagrangian angle at outer scales with suitable weights. Applying this result to a subset of the finite-time Lagrangian mean curvature flow singularities constructed in the companion paper [arXiv:2607.03152] and the infinite-time Lagrangian mean curvature flow singularities constructed by Tsai, Wood, and the second-named author [arXiv:2401.02228] then gives examples of both finite-time and infinite-time singularity formation with uniformly bounded mean curvature.
item.dc:creator: Maxwell Stolarski, Wei-Bo Su

item.title: Complex Martensitic Microstructures in ${\rm Ti}_{76}{\rm Nb}_{22}{\rm Al}_{2}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.06383v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We analyze the unusual microstructure resulting from the cubic to orthorhombic phase transformation in the shape-memory alloy ${\rm Ti}_{76}{\rm Nb}_{22}{\rm Al}_{2}$. This seems to represent an approximate experimental realization of a deformation having a finite number of incompatible deformation gradients, which has been known to exist only as a theoretical possibility. Because the middle eigenvalue $\gamma$ of the transformation strain is very close to 1, the phase transformation in this alloy takes place via nucleation of exact austenite-martensite interfaces rather than, as usual for other alloys, by classical austenite-martensite interfaces separating the austenite from a finely-twinned laminate of martensite. According to the moving mask approximation of Della Porta this leads to the question whether a microstructure can be formed from the set $H$ of the twelve matrices ${\mathbf V}_i$ on the martensite energy wells that are rank-one connected to the identity, even though these matrices are mutually incompatible. We show that when $\gamma=1$ and the transformation is volume preserving, such a microstructure is possible that does not deform the grain boundary. This is a consequence of $H$ forming a degenerate $T_{12}$ configuration in the sense of Kirchheim. In fact there are such microstructures supported on just 8 of the 12 matrices in $H$. However there is no deformation satisfying the same boundary condition whose gradient belongs to $H$ almost everywhere. An additional prediction, confirmed experimentally, is that the macroscopic deformation gradient equals the identity everywhere. We also analyse the approximate compatibility of the ${\mathbf V}_i$. Although mutually incompatible, they are nearly compatible, with some pairs much more nearly compatible than others, these pairs corresponding to interfaces that are more frequently observed.
item.dc:creator: John M. Ball, Francesco Della Porta, Tomonari Inamura

item.title: An ambient metric framework for sharp compactness of the constant $Q_{2N}$-curvature problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.06551v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a geometric method for studying $C^{2N}$-compactness of positive solutions to the constant $Q_{2N}$-curvature equation on closed Riemannian $n$-manifolds, for every integer $N\ge1$ and every dimension $n>2N$. Assuming the GJMS operator is invertible, its Green function is positive, and the positive mass condition holds, we establish sharp dimension ranges for the compactness of the set of all positive solutions with prescribed positive constant $Q_{2N}$-curvature. The largest dimension for compactness is $24$ for $N=1$ ([21]), $2N+20$ for $N=2,3$ ([11]), $2N+19$ for $N=4,5$, $2N+18$ for $N=6,7,8$, $2N+17$ for $9\le N\le17$, and $2N+16$ for all $N\ge18$. The constructions in [4,5,33,11] for $N=1,2,3$ and in the companion paper [12] for $N\ge4$ give noncompact examples in every dimension exceeding the corresponding compactness bound. We show that these $L^{\infty}$-unbounded examples can be chosen to satisfy the same operator and mass hypotheses, proving sharpness within this class. Our method relates the Pohozaev quadratic forms to the Hessian $D^2\mathscr{F}(g_c)$, where $\mathscr{F}$ is the volume-normalized total $Q_{2N}$-curvature functional and $g_c$ is the standard round metric on $\mathbb{S}^n$. The ambient metric argument of [12] supplies an explicit formula for $D^2\mathscr{F}(g_c)$ on transverse-traceless tensors. The York decomposition projects metric perturbations onto this space. The scalar--vector--tensor decomposition represents the Pohozaev quadratic forms by explicit finite-dimensional matrices. We prove that these matrices are positive definite throughout the stated dimension range, a crucial step in establishing compactness.
item.dc:creator: Liuwei Gong, Seunghyeok Kim, Juncheng Wei

item.title: Dual-Mode Extremum Seeking for Diffusion Systems with Boundary-Cost Feedback
item.description: arXiv:2611.06591v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Thermally tuned devices pose a basic control problem. A heater on one edge of a thin plate must hold a small element at an unknown optimal temperature, and the only signal available is the device's own performance. Boundary measurements of {such} an unknown performance objective can be used to tune a diffusion process without reconstructing its spatial state. This paper studies a dual-mode extremum-seeking controller for this setting, modeled as a semilinear diffusion equation on a square with nonuniform boundary actuation. The implementation contains two scalar states and exploits the leading attenuation and \rev{$\pi/4$} phase \rev{lag} of the diffusion response, a property shared by every periodically heated surface. It requires neither numerical plant coefficients nor the sign of the input gain. An energy estimate first establishes exponential stability of a coupled linear diffusion and controller model. A local bound on the remaining reaction and cost nonlinearities then yields stability and disturbance estimates for the averaged system. Complete kernel and boundary-trace arguments justify a change of coordinates that compares the implemented and averaged trajectories for all time. The resulting practical stability guarantee concerns the field, input bias, and sensitivity estimate, and is unaffected by a constant cost offset under corresponding filter initialization. At fixed dither amplitude, the residual state bound decreases with the inverse square root of frequency, while the ultimate cost bound decreases with its inverse. A thermal optical-filter example illustrates the predicted trends and the conservatism of the sufficient conditions.
item.dc:creator: Martin Guay, Denis Dochain

item.title: Uniqueness of Ricci flows from singular initial data
item.description: arXiv:2611.06814v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish uniqueness of Ricci flows with non-negative sectional curvatures and scaling invariant curvature bounds, assuming that the induced distance functions converge to the same initial distance function up to isometry. In the compact case, restricting the size of the initial singular set, we also establish uniqueness under suitable weaker conditions.
item.dc:creator: Laura Flower, Man-Chun Lee, Felix Schulze

item.title: Unique continuation estimates for Baouendi--Grushin equations on cylinders
item.description: arXiv:2401.17782v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove time-pointwise quantitative unique continuation estimates for the evolution operators associated to (fractional powers of) the Baouendi--Grushin operators on the cylinder $\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{T}^d$. Spectral inequalities are deduced, relating for functions from spectral subspaces associated to finite energy intervals their $L^2$-norm on the whole cylinder $\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb T^d$ to the $L^2$-norm on so-called thick subsets of $\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb T^d$. As a byproduct, we also obtain results on exact and approximate null-controllabilty for the corresponding evolution systems. This extends and complements results obtained recently by the authors and by Jaming and Wang.
item.dc:creator: Paul Alphonse, Albrecht Seelmann

item.title: The extension of traces for Sobolev mappings between manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2403.18738v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The compact Riemannian manifolds $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{N}$ for which the trace operator from the first-order Sobolev space of mappings $\smash{\dot{W}}^{1, p} (\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{N})$ to the fractional Sobolev-Slobodecki\u{\i} space $\smash{\smash{\dot{W}}^{1 - 1/p, p}} (\partial \mathcal{M}, \mathcal{N})$ is surjective when $1 < p < \dim \mathcal{M}$ are characterised. The traces are extended using a new construction which can be carried out assuming the absence of the known topological and analytical obstructions. When $p \ge \dim \mathcal{M}$ the same construction provides a Sobolev extension with linear estimates for maps that have a continuous extension, provided that the known analytical obstructions to such a control are not present.
item.dc:creator: Jean Van Schaftingen

item.title: On the Existence, Smoothness, and Order-Two Entire Extension of the Navier-Stokes Equations in Critical Fourier-Besov Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2405.07929v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish global existence, smoothness, and physical energy bounds for solutions to the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d \ge 3$) under a scaling-critical smallness condition in the homogeneous Fourier-Besov spaces $\mathscr{X}_p(\mathbb{R}^d)$, defined as the weak space $F \dot{B}^{\frac{d}{p'}-1}_{p,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for $1 < p \le \infty$ and $F \dot{B}^{-1}_{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ at the endpoint $p = 1$. By combining the nonassociative algebra of Riesz convolutions and spaces of functions dominated by Fourier-Caloric flows $\mathscr{V}(\lambda)$ with a Littlewood-Paley dyadic atomic decomposition, we prove that the Catalan Picard series converges globally whenever $\|\widehat{u^0}\|_{\mathscr{X}_p(\mathbb{R}^d)} < C\nu$. This threshold reaches the sharp boundary of well-posedness prior to norm inflation, strictly improves upon the classical Fujita-Kato $\dot{H}^{\frac{d}{2}-1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ condition, and admits explicit multiscale Schwartz initial data with arbitrarily large $\dot{H}^{\frac{d}{2}-1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and $H^k(\mathbb{R}^d)$ norms. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for positive times, the velocity and pressure fields admit an analytic extension to the complex domain $\mathbb{C}^d$, forming a smooth curve of entire vector fields of order two. Finally, for arbitrary initial data outside the critical ball, we employ fractional Riesz convolutions $*_\alpha$ ($0 < \alpha < 1$) to derive an explicit lower bound $T_{\max}(u^0) > 0$ on the lifespan of smooth, order-two entire solutions, establishing a sharp dichotomy between global continuation via viscous re-entry into the critical ball and a scaling-invariant lower blow-up rate.
item.dc:creator: Brian David Vasquez Campos

item.title: The superposition principle for the continuity equation with singular flux
item.description:
arXiv:2506.15333v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Representation results for absolutely continuous curves $\mu:[0,T]	o \mathcal{P}_p(\mathbb{R}^d)$, $p>1$, with values in the Wasserstein space $(\mathcal{P}_p(\mathbb{R}^d),W_p)$ of Borel probability measures in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with finite $p$-moment, provide a crucial tool to study evolutionary PDEs in a measure-theoretic setting. They are strictly related to the superposition principle for measure-valued solutions to the continuity equation. This paper addresses the extension of these results to the case $p=1$, and to curves $\mu:[0,+\infty)	o\mathcal{P}_1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ that are only of bounded variation in time: in the corresponding continuity equation, the flux measure $
u\in\mathcal{M}_{loc}([0,+\infty)	imes\mathbb{R}^{d};\mathbb{R}^{d})$ thus possesses a non-trivial singular part w.r.t. $\mu$ in addition to the absolutely continuous part featuring the velocity field. Firstly, we carefully address the relation between curves in ${m BV}_{loc}([0,+\infty);\mathcal{P}_1(\mathbb{R}^d))$ and solutions to the associated continuity equation, among which we select those with minimal singular (contribution to the) flux $
u$. We show that, with those distinguished solutions it is possible to associate an `auxiliary' continuity equation, in an augmented phase space, solely driven by its velocity field. For that continuity equation, a standard version of the superposition principle can be thus obtained. In this way, we derive a first probabilistic representation of the pair $(\mu,
u)$ solutions by projection over the time and space marginals. This representation involves Lipschitz trajectories in the augmented phase space, reparametrized in time and solving the characteristic system of ODEs. Finally, for the same pair $(\mu,
u)$ we also prove a superposition principle in terms of BV curves on the actual time interval, providing a fine description of their behaviour at jump points.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Almi, Riccarda Rossi, Giuseppe Savar\'e

item.title: Stability and asymptotic behaviour of one-dimensional solutions in cylinders
item.description: arXiv:2509.09648v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider positive one-dimensional solutions of a Lane-Emden relative Dirichlet problem in a cylinder and study their stability/instability properties as the energy varies with respect to domain perturbations. This depends on the exponent $p >1$ of the nonlinearity and we obtain results for $p$ close to 1 and for $p$ large. This is achieved by a careful asymptotic analysis of the one-dimensional solution as $p \to 1$ or $p \to \infty$, which is of independent interest. It allows to detect the limit profile and other qualitative properties of these solutions.
item.dc:creator: Francesca De Marchis, Lisa Mazzuoli, Filomena Pacella

item.title: Observability estimates for the Schr\"odinger equation on the equilateral triangle
item.description: arXiv:2509.24642v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove observability estimates for the Schr\"odinger equation posed on the equilateral triangle in the plane, under both Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions. No geometric control condition is required on the rough localization functions that we consider. This is the first result of this kind on a non-toric domain in the compact setting. Our strategy is to exploit Pinsky's tiling argument to deduce this result from observability estimates on rational twisted tori. These are obtained via propagation of singularities, adapting arguments from Burq and Zworski. The later require Strichartz estimates on such twisted rational tori, that we derive from Zygmund inequalities in the same geometric setting, also providing the sharp constant. Strichartz estimates on the equilateral triangle are also derived from this analysis.
item.dc:creator: Paul Alphonse, David Lafontaine

item.title: Operational Calculus for the nth-Level Prabhakar Type Fractional Derivative with Applications
item.description: arXiv:2512.21273v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This study investigates the nth-level Prabhakar fractional derivative, a generalization encompassing some well-known fractional derivatives. We establish its fundamental properties, particularly its relationship with the corresponding Prabhakar fractional integral. Furthermore, we develop Mikusinski-type operational calculus for this derivative, providing a framework for solving differential equations involving this operator. To illustrate its application, we present analytical solutions of two problems: a fractional order ordinary differential equation and the time fractional heat equation, both of which include the nth-level Prabhakar derivative.
item.dc:creator: Imtiaz Waheed, Erkinjon Karimov, Mujeeb ur Rehman

item.title: Normalized solutions of nonlinear magnetic Schr\"odinger equations on metric graphs
item.description: arXiv:2512.23321v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we first establish the theory of a magnetic Sobolev space $H^1_A(\mathcal{G},\mathbb{C})$ on metric graphs $\mathcal{G}$ and prove the self-adjointness of the associated magnetic Schr\"odinger operator. Then, in this setting, we investigate the existence and multiplicity of normalized solutions to nonlinear magnetic Schr\"odinger equations on compact metric graphs and on noncompact metric graphs with localized nonlinearities or nonlinearities acting on whole metric graphs, covering the mass-subcritical, mass-critical, and mass-supercritical cases.
item.dc:creator: Pietro d'Avenia, Zhentao He, Chao Ji

item.title: Dirac solitons in one-dimensional nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations
item.description: arXiv:2512.24089v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we study a family of one-dimensional stationary cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger (NLS) equations with periodic potentials and linear part displaying Dirac points in the dispersion relation. By introducing a suitable periodic perturbation, one can open a spectral gap around the Dirac-point energy. This allows to construct standing waves of the NLS equation whose leading-order profile is a modulation of Bloch waves by means of the components of a spinor solving an appropriate cubic nonlinear Dirac (NLD) equation. We refer to these solutions as Dirac solitons. Our analysis thus provides a rigorous justification for the use of the NLD equation as an effective model for the original NLS equation.
item.dc:creator: William Borrelli, Elena Danesi, Simone Dovetta, Lorenzo Tentarelli

item.title: The {\L}ojasiewicz-Simon inequality related to grain boundary motion and its applications
item.description: arXiv:2601.19226v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the {\L}ojasiewicz-Simon gradient inequality for the mathematical model of grain boundary motion. We first derive a curve shortening equation with time-dependent mobility, which guarantees the energy dissipation law for the grain boundary energy, including the difference between orientations of the constituent grains as a state variable. Next, we discuss the {\L}ojasiewicz-Simon gradient inequality for the grain boundary energy. Finally, we give applications of the inequality to the energy.
item.dc:creator: Masashi Mizuno, Ayumi Sakiyama, Keisuke Takasao

item.title: Probabilistically Strong Solutions to Stochastic Euler Equations
item.description: arXiv:2601.22073v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we establish the existence of probabilistically strong, measure-valued solutions for the stochastic incompressible Navier--Stokes equations with additive and transport noise. Considering the vanishing viscosity limit, we prove the convergence of these solutions to probabilistically strong, dissipative weak solutions to the stochastic incompressible Euler equations with additive and transport noise. Introducing the concept of energy-variational solutions in the stochastic context we are able to treat the nonlinearities without changing the probability space. This resolves the open problem of constructing, in three dimensions, probabilistically, strong solutions of the stochastic Euler equations as vanishing-viscosity limits on the prescribed stochastic basis. In addition, the constructed solutions satisfy the energy inequality and general $L^2$ initial data is treated.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Gess, Robert Lasarzik

item.title: Short-wave signal versus indirect prey-taxis
item.description: arXiv:2604.20469v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We address short-wave asymptotics for one class of quasi-linear second-order PDE systems involving the cross-diffusion described by the so-called Patlak-Keller-Segel law. It is common to employ these equations for modeling the predator-prey community with the prey-taxis, which means the interactions of two species of particles or cells through which the species called "predators" is capable of moving directionally while searching for the other species called "prey." However, we suppose the predators to be sensitive not to the prey density but to a cue produced by the prey. Additionally, the production of the cue is assumed to be sensitive to the intensity of an external field, which is independent of the community state. This is what we call the external signal. It can be due to the spatiotemporal inhomogeneity of the environment arising from natural or artificial reasons. We assume that the external signal takes a general short-wave form and construct a complete formal asymptotic expansion for the short-wave solutions (modulo solving a chain of the so-called slow systems) with no restrictions on the spatial dimension or kinetics of inter- or intra-specific reactions. Further, we apply the short-wave asymptotic to studying the stability or instability induced by the external signal following Kapitza's theory for the upside-down pendulum. Applying the general results to some special classes of external signals, we get examples of suppressing the taxical transport, examples of the robustness of the species equilibrium to the signal up to a very strong stabilization or, oppositely, destabilization and blurring the borderline in the parametric space between the areas of stability and instability of this equilibrium.
item.dc:creator: Andrey Morgulis, Karrar Malal

item.title: Steady Euler flows with contact discontinuities in infinitely long nozzles
item.description: arXiv:2607.04804v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate two-dimensional steady subsonic Euler flows with a contact discontinuity in infinitely long nozzles. An Euler--Lagrange transformation reduces the problem to a scalar quasilinear elliptic equation in divergence form on a fixed strip, with discontinuous coefficients and the contact discontinuity conditions incorporated into the weak formulation. By solving this elliptic problem, we establish existence, uniqueness, and regularity of the flow on the maximal interval of wall amplitudes containing the straight-nozzle configuration. These results apply to general piecewise smooth subsonic upstream data and dispense entirely with the monotonicity, convexity, and small-perturbation assumptions imposed in earlier studies. In particular, the contact discontinuity curve is of class $C^{2,\alpha}$. We further investigate the downstream asymptotic behavior and show, under the corresponding decay assumptions on the nozzle walls, that the convergence rate of the flow matches that of the walls.
item.dc:creator: Jun Chen, Xuemei Deng, Xiaoguang You

item.title: Tightness of and counterexamples to several quantum estimates
item.description: arXiv:2608.04411v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove here several tightness results for such quantum inequalities as 1) the comparison of operator norm and product norm of $d$-local hamiltonians, 2) Bohnenblust--Hille inequality for $d$-local hamiltonians, 3) for quantum Fourier entropy-influence conjecture. We give a deterministic prove of the sharpness of Bohnenblust--Hille exponent. We also discuss the quantum Aaronson--Ambainis conjecture in a special case of anti-commuting Pauli strings.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Slote, Alexander Volberg, Haonan Zhang

item.title: Global well-posedness for the four-dimensional repulsive Vlasov--Poisson system and for Vlasov--Riesz equations
item.description: arXiv:2609.09512v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish global classical well-posedness for the four-dimensional repulsive Vlasov--Poisson system, for every nonnegative \(f_0\in C_c^1(\mathbb{R}^8)\). We also prove global well-posedness for Vlasov equations with power-law interactions for \(d\ge4\). For every \(0<\alpha<3\), we treat both attractive and repulsive interactions with arbitrary nonnegative, compactly supported bounded initial data. Neither result requires a smallness assumption on the initial data. For attractive interactions, a virial argument yields finite-time breakdown for negative-energy solutions when \(3\le\alpha<d+1\). The global existence proofs combine estimates along characteristics, analysis in Lagrangian coordinates, and Serre's compensated integrability.
item.dc:creator: Emmanouil Katriadakis

item.title: A Critical Value for the Viscosity Coefficient: Triggering Oscillatory Traveling Waves in the Pseudo-parabolic Fisher-KPP Equation
item.description: arXiv:2609.34368v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The pseudo-parabolic term $u_{xxt}$ serves as a canonical example of higher-order viscosity that provides effective regularization while capturing the refined physical mechanism. How it alters the dynamics of prototype equations remains a fundamental issue, which is not yet fully understood. The goal of this paper is to show that this term induces a sharp transition in traveling wave structure, via studying the pseudo-parabolic Fisher-KPP equation $$ u_t - \tau u_{xxt} = D u_{xx} + u(1-u). $$ We completely characterize how the parameter ratio $\tau/D$ acts as a critical switch: it preserves the monotonic structure of classical traveling waves when $\tau/D \leq 1$, yet it triggers a qualitative shift to oscillatory traveling waves when $\tau/D > 1$. Numerical simulations support these findings. The threshold $\tau/D=1$ thus captures the dual role of the pseudo-parabolic term: it acts as a structure-preserving viscosity when small, but when large it reflects dominant capillary hysteresis, generating the oscillations that explain the saturation overshoot, a phenomenon that contradicts classical diffusion models yet is widely observed in two-phase flow.

item.title: Explicit sharp gradient stability of the $L^{p}$-Poincar\'e inequality and fundamental gaps for the Dirichlet $p$-Laplacian operator
item.description: arXiv:2610.27281v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we establish sharp gradient stability of the $L^{p}$-Poincar\'e inequality with explicit constants on bounded convex domains for any $1<p<\infty$. These estimates control the distance to the optimizers in the strongest possible norm with the optimal stability exponent $\max\{2,p\}$, exhibiting the same phenomenon initially observed by Figalli and Zhang [FZ22a] for the $L^p$-Sobolev inequality. In the case $1<p<2$, we also establish a sharp upper bound gradient stability estimate with an explicit constant and the optimal exponent $p$, matching the exponent obtained by Ignat and Zuazua [IZ26]. By extending the lower stability estimate to general bounded domains with $C^2$ boundary, we are able to confirm the conjecture posed by Fleckinger-Pell\'e and Tak\'a\v{c} [FPT02, Section 8]. Finally, we apply the stability inequality to obtain positive fundamental gap estimates in terms of the inradius for the Dirichlet $p$-Laplacian.

item.title: Whole-space eventual log-concavity and level-set geometry for the multidimensional Fisher-KPP equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.30702v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish eventual strict log-concavity and quantitative level-set curvature bounds for the Fisher-KPP equation $u_t=\Delta u+u-u^2$ in $\mathbb R^N$, $N\geq2$, with nontrivial, nonnegative, smooth compactly supported initial data. Specifically, there exist $T>1$ and $c>0$ such that $D_x^2\log u(t,x)\leq-(c/t)e^{-2(\sqrt2-1)t}\mathrm{Id}$ for all $t\geq T$ and $x\in\mathbb R^N$. Consequently, after a single waiting time, the solution has exactly one critical point, which is a nondegenerate global maximizer, and every positive level set below the maximum is smooth, closed, and strictly convex with positive principal curvatures. Moreover, for levels in any fixed closed interval $K\subset(0,1)$, the principal curvatures are uniformly bounded below by $(1-C\log t/t)/(2t)$ for all sufficiently large $t$. The proof combines one-sided second angular derivative estimates for the fixed-front region, absorptive comparison in the invaded interior, leading-edge barriers and blow-up arguments through the diffusive scale, and uniform Gaussian amplitude estimates in the exterior.
item.dc:creator: Xing Liang, Ziqi Zhen

item.title: Bubble Tree Convergence for Minimisers of a Regularised Baby-Skyrme Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.37457v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study degree $1$ minimisers $u: (\Sigma,g) \to S^2$ for a Baby-Skyrme model with a Sacks-Uhlenbeck regularisation term $E^{\alpha}(u) = \frac{1}{2} \int_{\Sigma} (1+\vert \nabla u \vert^2)^{\alpha+1} -1 dv_g$ and establish convergence of degree $1$ minimisers to a simple bubble tree as $\alpha \to 0$. We also obtain a new no-neck result for the classical Sacks-Uhlenbeck energy $E^{\alpha}$.

item.title: Lojasiewicz Estimates for a Regularised Baby-Skyrme Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.37499v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the structure of degree $1$ minimisers of a Baby-Skyrme energy of maps $u:\Sigma \to S^2$ regularised by a Sacks-Uhlenbeck perturbation, and we establish quantitative convergence rates to a simple bubble tree consisting of a single degree $1$ bubble and a constant base map.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Woodward

item.title: Revisiting Guo-Huang-Wang-Wei pointwise estimates for radial solutions to the fourth-order H\'enon equation in the punctured space
item.description: arXiv:2610.39134v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study pointwise estimates for positive, $C^4$-solution $u$ to the fourth-order H\'enon equation \[ \Delta^2 u = |x|^\sigma u^p \quad \text{in } \mathbf R^n \setminus \{0\} \] with $n \geq 5$, $p>1$, and $\sigma >-4 $. In an earlier work published in J. Anal. Math. 140 (2020) 371-394, Z. Guo, X. Huang, L. Wang, and J. Wei established the following pointwise estimate \[ -\Delta u \geq \frac 2{n-4} \frac{|\nabla u|^2}u + \sqrt{\frac {n(n-4)}{n^2-4}} u^\frac{n}{n-4} \quad \text{in } \mathbf R^n \setminus \{0\} \] for radial solutions to the critical, fourth-order Lane-Emden equation, namely $\sigma = 0$ and $p=(n+4)/(n-4)$. Inspired by this interesting result, we establish a similar pointwise inequality \[ -\Delta u \geq \frac 2{n-4} \frac{|\nabla u|^2}u + \sqrt{\frac 2{p+1- \frac 8{n(n-4)}}} |x|^{\frac \sigma 2} u^\frac{p+1}2 \quad \text{in } \mathbf R^n \setminus \{0\} \] for radial solutions to the fourth-order H\'enon equation in $\mathbf R^n \setminus \{0\}$ for any $\sigma \geq 0$ and $p \geq (n+4 + \sigma)/(n-4)$. We also show that the constant $2/(n-4)$ is sharp and that the thresholds $\sigma \geq 0$ and $p \geq (n+4 + \sigma)/(n-4)$ are necessary. As in our previous study on the case of $\mathbf R^n$, our proof is also based on the Bernstein technique via the maximum principle, hence appears to be simpler and more constructive. However, to avoid possible singularity at the origin, we develop a Bernstein technique in one-dimensional space, which is capable of handling equations in punctured spaces.

item.title: Stability threshold for 3D Boussinesq equations with rotation near the Couette flow and vertical stratified temperature
item.description: arXiv:2611.00964v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The most important features that distinguish fluid flow in the atmosphere and ocean are the effects of rotation and stratification, which are described by the Boussinesq equations with rotation. This paper examines the stability threshold at high Reynolds number $\mathbf{Re}$ for the 3D Boussinesq equations with rotation near Couette flow and a vertical stratified temperature. For the zero modes, the combined effects of rotation and stratification sustain velocity-temperature oscillations with frequencies bounded away from zero. In the stable rotational regime, rotation suppresses the linear growth associated with the lift-up effect, while stratification sustains oscillations in the double zero modes. Although the zero modes dynamics are not fully dispersive, we exploit the structure of the oscillatory phases and cancellations in the equations to obtain a modified energy estimate for the entire zero modes system. Combining this estimate with enhanced dissipation and inviscid damping of the nonzero modes, we establish a bound for the stability threshold, with order $\mathbf{Re}^{-2/3}(1+\log\mathbf{Re})^{-1-a_0}$ for any fixed $a_0\in(0,1/2)$.

item.title: Sharp Weighted Hardy-Trace Inequalities for Homogeneous Magnetic Potentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.03860v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a sharp magnetic improvement of the family of weighted inequalities on the upper half-space $\mathbb{R}^{N+1}_+$ that interpolate between the Hardy inequality and the trace Hardy inequality. The magnetic potentials are of Aharonov-Bohm type, $\mathbf{A}(x)=|x|^{-1}\boldsymbol{a}(x/|x|)$, where the tangential field $\boldsymbol{a}$ may be singular on a closed subset of the sphere. We compute the sharp constant explicitly: it is given by the constant of the corresponding nonmagnetic inequality, evaluated in a virtual dimension that depends on the first eigenvalue of the magnetic Laplacian on the sphere. In particular, the magnetic trace Hardy constant strictly exceeds its Euclidean value whenever this eigenvalue is positive. The proof rests on a ground state representation of the deficit, which also shows that the sharp constant is not attained in the energy space. As a consequence, we obtain the sharp Hardy inequality for the fractional powers $(-\Delta_{\mathbf{A}})^\sigma$, $0<\sigma<1$, of the magnetic Laplacian: the constant is the same on smooth functions supported away from the singular set and on the form domain of $(-\Delta_{\mathbf{A}})^\sigma$, and it is not attained. Examples include the planar Aharonov-Bohm potential with nonintegral flux and, in dimension three, the Aharonov-Bohm potential and the Dirac monopole.
item.dc:creator: Hern\'an Castro, Andres Zuniga

item.title: Foundations on k-contact geometry
item.description: arXiv:2409.11001v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: $k$-Contact geometry is a generalisation of contact geometry to analyse field theories. As a main goal, we develop an approach to $k$-contact geometry based on distributions that are distributionally maximally non-integrable and admit, locally, $k$ commuting supplementary Lie symmetries: the $k$-contact distributions. More specifically, we investigate the existence of Reeb vector fields for $k$-contact distributions, $k$-contact Lie groups are defined and studied, and, after analysing compact manifolds, a Weinstein conjecture for a product of $k$ compact contact manifolds is discussed. Polarisations for $k$-contact distributions are introduced and it is shown that a polarised $k$-contact distribution is locally diffeomorphic to the Cartan distribution of the first-order jet bundle over a fibre bundle of rank $k$. We relate $k$-contact manifolds to presymplectic and $k$-symplectic manifolds on fibre bundles of larger dimension and define types of submanifolds in $k$-contact geometry. We study Hamilton--De Donder--Weyl equations on $k$-contact Lie groups. A theory of $k$-contact Hamiltonian vector fields is developed, and we describe characteristics of Lie symmetries for first-order partial differential equations in a $k$-contact Hamiltonian manner. We use our techniques to analyse Hamilton--Jacobi and Dirac equations, types of Engel and Goursat distributions, physical problems, and control systems. The work also presents introductory results so as to make it more self-contained.
item.dc:creator: Javier de Lucas, Xavier Rivas, Tomasz Sobczak

item.title: Semiclassical resonances under local magnetic fields
item.description: arXiv:2604.17854v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study resonances for the semiclassical magnetic Laplacian in the full plane with a compactly supported magnetic field in the framework of semiclassical complex scaling and black box scattering theory. Assuming that the magnetic field is locally constant, we prove the existence of semiclassical resonances near the Landau levels with exponentially small imaginary parts. We also prove that resonances emerge from a magnetic step discontinuity along a curved interface or a non-degenerate magnetic well, and in the vicinity of anharmonic Landau levels if the field has an isolated zero.
